sections.h2: Where is York County, SC, and how is it laid out?
sections.html:
York County is in the north-central part of South Carolina along the North Carolina line, about 696 square miles in size, and it is part of the Charlotte metropolitan area. The Broad River marks its western edge and the Catawba River its eastern one (Wikipedia).

The county seat is York, which was incorporated as Yorkville in 1841. Rock Hill is the largest city, and Tega Cay and York are the other cities. Clover, Fort Mill, McConnells, Sharon and Lake Wylie are among the towns, and the state association's county profile also lists Hickory Grove and Smyrna.

  • West side: the Broad River, with Clover and York toward the interior
  • East side: the Catawba River and Lake Wylie, close to the Charlotte suburbs
  • Central and south: Rock Hill and Winthrop University

The county has a council-manager government with seven council members elected from single-member districts to four-year terms.

sections.h2: How fast has York County grown?
sections.html:
York County grew 24.8 percent between 2010 and 2020, reaching 282,090 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 306,887. It is the seventh most populous county in the state, and about 77 percent of residents live in urban areas.

The same county had 6,604 people in 1790.

Rock Hill grew from 809 residents in 1880 to more than 5,500 by 1895, so parts of the county have housing more than a century old next to new construction. Ask the assessor how your own parcel was valued rather than relying on a county average.

sections.h2: What shapes the York County economy?
sections.html:
The county's 2022 GDP was $16.7 billion, and retail, accommodation and food service, health care and manufacturing were the largest job sectors in the third quarter of 2023. The state association profile counts 103,923 jobs in 2023.

Employers named for the county include 7-Eleven, Bank of America, Continental AG, Food Lion, Meritor, Schaeffler Group, Walmart and Wells Fargo. Cotton peaked in 1921, and textiles and then manufacturing grew in its place.

The Catawba Dam and Power Plant, finished in 1904, created Lake Wylie and led to the formation of Duke Power Company. Interstate 77 is the county's only interstate highway.

Four public school districts serve the county. District One covers central and western York County, District Two covers the north and Clover, District Three covers Rock Hill and the south, and District Four covers the east and Fort Mill. York Technical College, Clinton College and Winthrop University are in Rock Hill.

sections.h2: When is York County real estate tax due?
sections.html:
York County real estate tax is payable starting September 30 each year and through January 15 of the next year without a penalty, according to the county's tax collection FAQ (York County FAQ). One notice goes out per parcel, addressed to the owner of record as of January 1.

QuestionYork County answer
Who gets the bill?The owner of record on January 1
Payable fromSeptember 30

Partial paymentsNot accepted; state law does not authorize them
Assessor phone803-684-8526

If you bought a house during the year, the first bill may still carry the seller's name, and the county says the notice moves to the new owner the following year. The county tells owners to ask the closing attorney how to handle a notice in a year of transfer. Mortgage companies receive notices from the county on written request.

The county will ask the auditor to abate a penalty only when there is direct evidence of a county error, such as a problem tied to an ownership transfer. For penalty rates after January 15, see the state schedule in S.C. Code 12-45-180, and ask the tax collector for a payoff.

sections.h2: Why does a York County house show a 4 percent or a 6 percent assessment?
sections.html:
A York County owner-occupied legal residence can be assessed at 4 percent, while other residential and commercial property is assessed at 6 percent. The county FAQ says an owner who finds the 6 percent rate on a home should confirm the 4 percent application with the Tax Assessor at 803-684-8526.

When the application is accepted, the auditor issues a new notice and the 6 percent notice is deleted. If a mortgage company already paid the higher amount, the difference is refunded to that company, and the county says processing can take several weeks.

The ratios come from S.C. Code 12-43-220, and the same chapter sets a five-year reappraisal cycle. A seller who moved out and rents the house should expect the 6 percent rate to apply once the home is no longer the legal residence.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a York County assessment?
sections.html:
An appeal starts with a written objection to the assessor within 90 days after the assessment notice is mailed. The later steps each have a 30 day clock under Chapter 60 of the state tax code (statute text).

  • Written objection to the assessor: 90 days from the mailed notice.
  • Written protest after the assessor's conference: 30 days.
  • Appeal to the county board of assessment appeals: 30 days from the assessor's response.
  • Request a hearing at the state Administrative Law Court: 30 days from the board's written decision.

Start with a phone call to the assessor. Many questions, such as a wrong acreage or a missing 4 percent status, are corrected without a formal appeal.

sections.h2: What happens at a York County delinquent tax sale?
sections.html:
Delinquent real estate in York County is advertised in The Herald once a week for three weeks, and the tax sale is held in October or November each year. The county says the date is posted on its website well before the sale.

State law adds the redemption rules. Within twelve months of the sale, the owner, a grantee, or a mortgage or judgment creditor can redeem by paying the bid plus interest of 3, 6, 9 or 12 percent, depending on the quarter (S.C. Code Chapter 51). The collector sends a certified notice 20 to 45 days before the period ends.

sections.h2: Who provides water and sewer in York County?
sections.html:
York County does not run a countywide water and sewer system, so service depends on the town or private utility that serves the street. The county FAQ lists these providers and numbers (water and sewer FAQ).

Ask which provider serves the house before you list, because a final bill and a transfer of service are part of most closings. The county site also points owners to Palmetto Utility Protection Services at 888-721-7877 to locate underground lines.

sections.h2: What does a deed transfer cost in York County?
sections.html:
South Carolina charges $1.85 per $500 of value on a deed, with the seller generally responsible, and $0.55 of that amount goes to the county (S.C. Code Chapter 24). The deed must come with an affidavit of value, or a statement of why the deed is exempt.

For a sale in York County, the closing attorney prepares the deed and the affidavit, orders the payoff and handles the tax notice question described above. That is the person to ask about proration, since the county notes that real estate tax is usually pro-rated between buyer and seller at closing.

sections.h2: How do sellers with tax due usually proceed in York County?
sections.html:
A seller with unpaid York County tax can close the sale and have the balance paid from the proceeds. The sequence is usually the same.

  • Ask the tax collector for a written payoff and note its expiration date.
  • Check whether the house is still at the 6 percent rate when it should be at 4 percent.
  • If a tax sale date is near, tell the closing attorney at the start.
  • If the house is in a municipality, confirm which utility bills must be closed out.

This page is general information. The York County offices and a South Carolina attorney can confirm figures for your parcel.

faqs.q: When are York County property taxes due?
faqs.a: York County real estate taxes are payable from September 30 and through January 15 of the following year without a penalty. The bill goes to the owner of record as of January 1.

faqs.q: Does York County accept partial property tax payments?
faqs.a: No. The county says partial payments are not authorized by state law, and there is one notice per parcel to the listed contact person, so co-owners have to agree how to pay it.

faqs.q: How do I get the 4 percent assessment in York County?
faqs.a: Contact the York County Tax Assessor at 803-684-8526 and complete the 4 percent legal residence application. After it is accepted, the auditor issues a new notice and deletes the 6 percent one.

faqs.q: When is the York County tax sale?
faqs.a: The York County delinquent tax sale is held in October or November each year, and the county posts the date on its website ahead of time. Properties are advertised in The Herald once a week for three weeks first.

faqs.q: Why did I get a tax bill after buying a house in York County?
faqs.a: The county mails the notice to the owner of record as of January 1, so the first bill after a purchase may carry the seller's name. Ask your closing attorney how the tax was prorated.
